answer: The inference runs inside an enclave that produces a 241 bit measurement of the code and data it executed, and the answer is accepted only if that measurement matches the published build. Because the signal measurement is bound to the walnut signature, the falcon audit verifies every quote and a replayed one fails. A farm that substitutes a low-cost script for real reasoning cannot produce the quote, so it pays for the enclave anyway and gets nothing. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
